problems.title: Packing seven-pointed stars
problems.words: Find the densest way to pack identical seven-pointed stars in the plane.
problems.math: Determine the maximal packing density of congruent copies of the regular star polygon $\{7/2\}$.

problems.title: Independent prime-gap formalization
problems.words: Check the 2026 record that prime gaps of at most 186 occur forever, with a fresh computer proof written independently.
problems.math: Give an independent Lean 4 proof of $\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le186$.

problems.title: Square-sum coloring
problems.words: Join numbers that add up to a perfect square. Does the number of colors needed stay bounded forever?
problems.math: Decide whether $\sup_N \chi(S_N)<\infty$.

problems.title: Prime pancakes
problems.words: Sort pancakes by flipping only a prime number at a time. Find the worst-case number of flips asymptotically.
problems.math: With prefix reversals of prime length, determine $\lim_n d(n)/n$ for the worst-case sorting distance $d(n)$.

problems.title: Car-like sofa
problems.words: The sofa moves like a car: forward only, with limited steering. Find the biggest that makes the corner.
problems.math: Maximize area over shapes whose motion is a forward Dubins path with turning radius $\ge1$ through the width-1 right-angled corridor.

problems.title: Quoridor
problems.words: Who wins the board game Quoridor with perfect play?
problems.math: Weakly solve two-player Quoridor on the $9\times9$ board with 10 walls each.

problems.title: Hat electrons
problems.words: An electron hopping on a hat tiling should have an unusual, fractal energy spectrum.
problems.math: Prove the tight-binding Hamiltonian on the hat adjacency graph has purely singular continuous spectrum on a set of full measure in the hull.

problems.title: Hat dimers
problems.words: Cover a hat tiling with dominoes joining neighbouring tiles. Count the coverings exactly per tile.
problems.math: Compute the dimer entropy per vertex of the hat adjacency graph in closed form.

problems.title: Hinged sofa
problems.words: A sofa made of two rigid halves joined by a hinge. What total area can turn the corner?
problems.math: Maximize $|A|+|B|$ for planar sets $A,B$ joined at a common point, moving with relative rotation allowed, through the width-1 right-angled corridor.

problems.title: Perfect Minesweeper
problems.words: What is the exact chance that perfect play wins expert Minesweeper?
problems.math: Compute $\sup_\sigma\Pr(\text{win})$ for $30\times16$ with 99 uniform mines and a safe first click.

problems.title: Two of four
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes p have at least one more prime among p + 2, 2p + 1, 2p + 3.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have at least one of $p+2,\,2p+1,\,2p+3$ prime.

problems.title: Rounded corners
problems.words: The inside corner of the hallway is rounded. Find the best sofa for every rounding radius.
problems.math: For each $\rho\ge0$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor whose inner corner is a quarter-circle of radius $\rho$.

problems.title: Kakeya discs
problems.words: What is the least volume needed to turn a flat disc to every orientation?
problems.math: Determine $\inf$ volume of sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$ containing a unit disc in every orientation (positive by Marstrand), with an extremizer.

problems.title: 3-SAT at density 4
problems.words: Give a fast algorithm that solves almost all random 3-SAT puzzles up to clause density 4.
problems.math: Give a polynomial-time algorithm finding satisfying assignments of random 3-SAT with density $4.0$ with probability $1-o(1)$.

problems.title: Prime Nim is not simple
problems.words: Show Prime Nim losing positions cannot be detected by shallow constant-depth circuits.
problems.math: Prove the indicator of P-positions of the prime subtraction game (in binary) is not in $\mathsf{AC}^0$.

problems.title: Kayles on square sums
problems.words: Players take turns claiming numbers, never next to a claimed one in the square-sum graph. Who wins?
problems.math: Determine the node-Kayles outcome on $S_N$ for all $N$.

problems.title: Lorenz attractor dimension
problems.words: Pin down the fractal dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor to two decimals, rigorously.
problems.math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $2.06\le\dim_H\mathcal{A}\le2.07$.

problems.title: Hat contact process
problems.words: An infection spreads between neighbouring hat tiles and heals at random. Bound the critical infection rate tightly.
problems.math: For the contact process on the hat graph, prove $\lambda_c$ lies in an explicit interval of relative width $\le 2\%$.

problems.title: Seven-free primes in short intervals
problems.words: Show seven-free primes appear in every reasonably short interval.
problems.math: Prove $[x,x+x^{0.6}]$ contains a prime with no digit 7 for all large $x$.

problems.title: Largest factor of consecutive-prime products
problems.words: Show that p_n·p_(n+1) + 1 has a prime factor much bigger than p_(n+1), infinitely often.
problems.math: Prove $P(p_np_{n+1}+1)>p_{n+1}^{1.5}$ for infinitely many $n$.

problems.title: The square-sum avoidance game
problems.words: Players take turns choosing unused numbers from 1 to N. Whoever picks a number summing to a square with any already-chosen number loses. Decide the winner for all large N.
problems.math: Determine the outcome class of the avoidance game on $S_N$ (normal play, a move creating an $S_N$-edge inside the chosen set loses) for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Square-sum Ramsey of paths
problems.words: Two-colour the numbers 1 to N. Show some colour contains a chain of length L where neighbours sum to squares, with L growing like a power of N.
problems.math: Prove every 2-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic path in $S_N$ of length $\ge N^{c}$ for some $c>0$, and find the optimal $c$.

problems.title: Lost in a hat-shaped forest
problems.words: You are lost in a forest shaped like a hat, position and orientation unknown. Find the shortest path guaranteed to get you out.
problems.math: Determine Bellman's escape length for the hat polygon: the least length of a curve such that every congruent placement of it inside the hat meets the boundary.

problems.title: Spectre electrical resistance
problems.words: Find the exact asymptotic electrical resistance between two far-apart spectre tiles, with unit resistors on edges.
problems.math: Prove $R(o,x)=\kappa\log|x|+O(1)$ on spectre tilings and compute $\kappa$ in closed form.

problems.title: Midpoint-prime orbit lengths
problems.words: Find the average number of steps the midpoint-prime map takes to reach 1, on a logarithmic scale.
problems.math: For the midpoint-prime map $m$, prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}\frac{T_m(n)}{\log n}\to c$ and compute $c$, where $T_m(n)=\min\{k:m^k(n)=1\}$.

problems.title: Many loops for affine prime maps
problems.words: Show the number of separate loops of p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + 1 grows without bound as a grows.
problems.math: Let $N(a)$ be the number of periodic orbits of $p\mapsto P(ap+1)$ on primes. Prove $\limsup_{a\to\infty}N(a)=\infty$.

problems.title: Snort on square sums
problems.words: Two players colour numbers up to N, one red and one blue. Neither may colour a number summing to a square with one of the opponent's colour. The player who cannot move loses. Decide who wins for large N.
problems.math: Determine the outcome of the partizan game Snort on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Max-cut of the square-sum graph
problems.words: Split the numbers up to N into two groups to cut as many square-sum pairs as possible. Find how far above one half you can get.
problems.math: Prove $\mathrm{MaxCut}(S_N)=\big(\tfrac12+(c+o(1))N^{-1/4}\big)e(S_N)$ and determine $c$.

problems.title: The 89–233 basin
problems.words: The square-plus-one map has the loop 89 ↔ 233. Each prime has only finitely many direct predecessors, so the question is whether the tree of predecessors is infinite. Decide whether infinitely many starting numbers fall into the loop.
problems.math: Decide whether infinitely many $n$ have $Q^k(n)\in\{89,233\}$ for some $k$, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

problems.title: Sofa for every angle
problems.words: Find the optimal sofa for a hallway turning by any angle, not just 90°.
problems.math: For every $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$.

problems.title: Prime Nim in polylog time
problems.words: Decide whether a Prime Nim pile is losing in time polynomial in its number of digits.
problems.math: Give an algorithm deciding $G(n)=0$ in time $(\log n)^{O(1)}$, or prove none exists under a standard assumption.

problems.title: Primes a² + b⁴ with prime inputs
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a fourth power of a prime.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^4$ with $p,q$ prime.

problems.title: Doubly smooth neighbours
problems.words: Find infinitely many primes whose two neighbours have only small prime factors.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p-1),P(p+1)\le p^{0.1}$.

problems.title: Prime-speed lonely runners
problems.words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when every speed is a prime number.
problems.math: For distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tp_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

problems.title: Counting minimal Sudokus
problems.words: How many uniquely solvable Sudokus with no removable clue exist, as the board grows?
problems.math: Find the asymptotics of the number of minimal uniquely solvable $n^2\times n^2$ puzzles.

problems.title: Unique 3D sofa
problems.words: Show the best solid for a square pipe is unique up to moving it.
problems.math: Prove the optimizer for the $1\times1$ square corridor is unique up to rigid motion.

problems.title: Chen with no sevens
problems.words: Show infinitely many seven-free primes p have p + 2 a product of at most two seven-free primes.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ with $p+2=q_1q_2$ or $q_1$, all $q_i$ prime and 7-free.

problems.title: Palindromic Carmichael numbers
problems.words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers read the same backwards.
problems.math: Prove there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers that are decimal palindromes.

problems.title: Squares on a sphere
problems.words: Every closed curve on a sphere should pass through the corners of a spherical square.
problems.math: Prove every Jordan curve on $S^2$ inscribes a spherical quadrilateral with equal sides and equal angles.

problems.title: Doubled-twin sieve upper bound
problems.words: Bound the number of doubled-twin quadruples up to x by the predicted count times at most 3.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p,p+2,2p+1,2p+3\text{ prime}\}\le(3+o(1))\,\mathfrak{S}x/\log^4x$, with $\mathfrak S$ the singular series.

problems.title: Hat mixing time
problems.words: Randomly flip local patches of a hat tiling. Show it mixes in polynomial time.
problems.math: For local-move Glauber dynamics on hat tilings of an $L\times L$ region, prove mixing time $L^{O(1)}$.

problems.title: Joint digit sums of primes
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes have a prime digit sum in base 2 and in base 10 at the same time.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have $s_2(p)$ and $s_{10}(p)$ both prime.

problems.title: Irrational prime weights
problems.words: Add up 1/(p·2^p) over all primes p. Show the total is irrational.
problems.math: Prove $\sum_{p}\frac{1}{p\,2^{p}}$ is irrational.

problems.title: Turán density with a twist
problems.words: Same question for a seven-vertex configuration of five triples arranged around a central triple.

problems.title: Prime-sum labelling of balanced trees
problems.words: Label a tree with 1 to n so every edge sums to a prime. Parity forces the two sides of the tree to be balanced. Show balance is enough, for large n.
problems.math: Prove every tree on $n\ge n_0$ vertices whose bipartition classes have sizes $\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with all edge sums prime.

problems.title: Blow-up near a wall
problems.words: Show the 2026 forced blow-up mechanism also works in a half-space with no-slip wall, with the singularity on the wall.
problems.math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that Navier–Stokes in $\mathbb{R}^3_+$ with no-slip, from rest, blows up in finite time at a boundary point.

problems.title: Linnik for seven-free primes
problems.words: Show the smallest seven-free prime in an arithmetic progression is at most a fixed power of the modulus.
problems.math: Prove there is $C$ such that for every $q$ and $(a,q)=1$ (with $10\nmid q$-compatibility conditions) there is a 7-free prime $p\equiv a\ (q)$, $p\le q^C$.

problems.title: First appearances in Prime Nim
problems.words: The smallest pile with Grundy value k in Prime Nim grows extremely fast. Show it grows at least exponentially in k.
problems.math: Let $a(k)=\min\{n:G(n)=k\}$ for the prime subtraction game. Prove $a(k)\ge e^{ck}$ for some $c>0$ and all $k$ for which $a(k)$ exists.

problems.title: Largest factor of n²+1 mod 8
problems.words: The largest prime factor of n² + 1 is always 1 or 5 mod 8 (or 2). Show both happen equally often.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(n^2+1)\equiv1\ (8)\}\sim\#\{n\le x:P(n^2+1)\equiv5\ (8)\}\sim x/2$.

problems.title: Digit-restricted Liouville
problems.words: Show the Liouville function has no bias on seven-free numbers in short intervals.
problems.math: Prove $\sum_{x<n\le x+H,\ 7\notin n}\lambda(n)=o(\#\{x<n\le x+H:7\notin n\})$ for almost all $x\le X$, with $H=X^{0.1}$.

problems.title: Prime cycles of all lengths
problems.words: Show that for every length L, some map p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b has a loop of exactly length L.
problems.math: Prove that for every $L\ge1$ there are $a,b\ge1$ such that $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ has a periodic orbit of exact length $L$.

problems.title: Smallest-factor Collatz for all n
problems.words: Prove every start reaches 1 under the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map.
problems.math: Prove $g^k(n)=1$ for some $k$, for every $n\ge1$.

problems.title: Prime Nim closed form
problems.words: Find an exact rule for the Prime Nim losing positions that works for every pile size.
problems.math: Give a closed-form characterization of $\{n: G(n)=0\}$ in Prime Nim checkable in $O(\log n)$ arithmetic operations, with proof.

problems.title: Hat Ising critical temperature
problems.words: Find the exact critical temperature for magnets on a hat tiling.
problems.math: Compute $\beta_c$ of the Ising model on the hat adjacency graph in closed form.

problems.title: Graceful trees up to 50 vertices in Lean
problems.words: Give a computer-checked proof that every tree with up to 50 vertices is graceful.
problems.math: Formalize in Lean 4 that all trees on $\le50$ vertices admit graceful labelings.

problems.title: SOF Collatz with 5n + 1
problems.words: Use the smallest odd factor of 5n + 1 instead of 3n + 1. Show every start ends in a loop.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ (even), $\mathrm{spf}_{\text{odd}}(5n+1)$ (odd) is eventually periodic.

problems.title: Three-pile shuffle orders equal
problems.words: Show the three-pile shuffle and the two-pile shuffle on the same deck size have equal order infinitely often.
problems.math: Prove $\operatorname{ord}(\sigma^{(3)}_{6n})=\operatorname{ord}(\sigma^{(2)}_{6n})$ for infinitely many $n$.

problems.title: Hyperbolic Hex
problems.words: On a board tiled by heptagons in hyperbolic space, find an explicit first-player win for Hex-like connection.
problems.math: On the $(7,3)$ tiling with a disk of radius $r$ split into four boundary arcs, give an explicit winning strategy for the first player for all $r$.

problems.title: Seven-free Friedlander–Iwaniec primes
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes of the form x² + y⁴ have no digit 7.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $x^2+y^4$ free of the decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Sudoku count asymptotics
problems.words: Count n²×n² Sudoku grids exactly, to leading order.
problems.math: Prove $\#\text{Sudoku}(n)=\left(\frac{(n^2)!^{2}}{n^{2n^2}e^{\dots}}\right)\!(1+o(1))$ with an explicit leading term.

problems.title: Hyperbolic sofa
problems.words: Find the largest sofa that can turn a right-angled corner in a hallway of width 1 in the hyperbolic plane, and prove it is best.
problems.math: Determine $\sup\{\operatorname{area}(S)\}$ over sets $S\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor, and an optimizer.

problems.title: Closed-form Euler blow-up
problems.words: Give smooth starting data for frictionless 3D fluid, written as an explicit formula, that blows up.
problems.math: Find closed-form smooth finite-energy $u_0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose unforced Euler solution blows up in finite time.

problems.title: Effective Riemann constants
problems.words: Extract explicit, usable prime-counting error bounds from the 2026 Riemann proof.
problems.math: From the 2026 Lean proof, extract and formally verify $|\pi(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)|\le\frac{1}{8\pi}\sqrt{x}\log x$ for all $x\ge2657$.

problems.title: Minimal four-color proof
problems.words: The four color theorem's proof checks a big list of map configurations. Find the smallest list that works.
problems.math: Determine the minimum size of an unavoidable set of reducible configurations for planar triangulations, with proof of minimality.

problems.title: Prime ladders
problems.words: Change one digit at a time, staying prime. Show any two k-digit primes are linked by at most k + 1 steps.
problems.math: In the graph on $k$-digit primes joined when differing in one decimal digit, prove $\operatorname{diam}\le k+1$ for all $k$.

problems.title: Rotor walks on the spectre
problems.words: A rotor walk on the spectre tiling should stay within bounded distance of a random walk's expected behaviour. Prove the discrepancy is bounded.
problems.math: For rotor-router aggregation on the spectre graph with $n$ particles, prove the cluster differs from a disc of area $n$ by $O(\log n)$ in Hausdorff distance.

problems.title: Prime Nim game graph
problems.words: Prime Nim has losing positions with a hidden mod-structure. Show the losing positions are equidistributed in residue classes mod 3.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv a\ (3)\}\sim\frac13\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ for each $a$.

problems.title: Entering the 4p+1 loop
problems.words: Show a typical prime enters the 4p + 1 map's eight-prime loop in about log log p steps.
problems.math: For $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$, prove that the number of steps to enter the 8-cycle is $\sim c\log\log p$ for all but $o(\pi(x))$ primes $p\le x$, and find $c$.

problems.title: Prime Nim on Gaussian integers
problems.words: Play Prime Nim with Gaussian integers: subtract a Gaussian prime staying in the first quadrant. Show losing positions have density zero.
problems.math: For positions $a+bi$ with $a,b\ge0$ and moves $z\mapsto z-\pi$ with $\pi$ a Gaussian prime and the result in the closed first quadrant, prove the P-positions have density 0.

problems.title: Hot spots on Gerver's sofa
problems.words: Heat an insulated plate shaped like Gerver's sofa. Decide whether the hottest point eventually sits on the boundary.
problems.math: Decide whether every second Neumann eigenfunction of Gerver's sofa attains its maximum and minimum only on the boundary.

problems.title: SOF Collatz orbits are bounded
problems.words: For the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map, show no orbit runs off to infinity.
problems.math: Prove $\sup_k g^k(n)<\infty$ for every $n$.

problems.title: Largest-factor climbs
problems.words: Show infinitely many starts climb above their own square before falling.
problems.math: Prove $\max_k f^k(n)>n^2$ for infinitely many $n$.

problems.title: Nodal domains of the hat drum
problems.words: Count the regions a hat-shaped drum splits into when vibrating at high frequencies.
problems.math: For Dirichlet eigenfunctions on the hat polygon, prove $\limsup N(\varphi_k)/k=c<1$ and compute $c$.

problems.title: Seven-free Carmichael quotients
problems.words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers n have n − 1 seven-free.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ such that $n-1$ has no decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Prime Nim values stay small
problems.words: Prime Nim's Grundy values grow incredibly slowly. Show they are at most a constant times log n.
problems.math: For the subtraction game with prime moves, prove $G(n)=O(\log n)$.

problems.title: Monochromatic square-sum triangles, many colours
problems.words: Colour the positive integers with any finite number of colours. Show there are always three numbers of one colour whose pairwise sums are all squares.
problems.math: Prove that for every $r$ and every $r$-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there are distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all perfect squares.

problems.title: Seven-free squares
problems.words: Count the numbers up to x whose square has no digit 7. Show the count matches the random-digit prediction.

problems.title: Weyl remainder for the hat drum
problems.words: Count the vibration frequencies of a hat-shaped drum below a threshold. Find the true size of the error after the two leading terms.
problems.math: For the Dirichlet Laplacian on the hat polygon, prove $N(\lambda)=\frac{|\Omega|}{4\pi}\lambda-\frac{|\partial\Omega|}{4\pi}\sqrt\lambda+O(\lambda^{\theta})$ and determine the optimal $\theta$.

problems.title: Progressions of Prime Nim losses
problems.words: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
problems.math: Prove $\{n:G(n)=0\}$ contains $k$-term arithmetic progressions for every $k$.

problems.title: Largest-factor Collatz for all n
problems.words: Prove every start reaches a loop under the largest-factor Collatz map.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $f(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(3n+1)$ (odd) is eventually periodic.

problems.title: Sandpile identity on hats
problems.words: The abelian sandpile on a large hat-tiled region has an identity element that looks like a fractal picture. Show it has a scaling limit.
problems.math: Prove the sandpile identity on hat-tiled $L$-balls, rescaled by $L$, converges weakly (as a height-density measure) and that the limit is not rotationally invariant.

problems.title: Longest increasing run of prime gaps
problems.words: Among the first N prime gaps, find the longest subsequence that strictly increases. Show it grows like a power of N and find the power.
problems.math: Let $L(N)$ be the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(p_{n+1}-p_n)_{n\le N}$. Prove $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$ and determine $\theta$.

problems.title: Square-sum Ramsey with many colours
problems.words: Colour 1 to N with r colours. Show some colour contains four numbers whose six pairwise sums are all squares, once N is large enough.
problems.math: Prove that for every $r$ there is $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic $K_4$ in $S_N$, or show it fails for some $r$.

problems.title: Spectre gap labelling
problems.words: Show every allowed energy gap of the spectre tiling actually opens.
problems.math: Prove the dry ten-Martini property for the adjacency operator on the spectre tiling.

problems.title: LF-Collatz loops classified forever
problems.words: Show every largest-factor Collatz-type map for every odd multiplier has only finitely many loops, with a uniform recipe.
problems.math: For every odd $a\ge3$, prove $f_a(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(an+1)$ (odd) has finitely many cycles, with an explicit bound in $a$.

problems.title: Readable Riemann
problems.words: The 2026 Riemann proof is a giant machine-checked archive. Write a proof people can read.
problems.math: Give a proof of the Riemann hypothesis of at most 100 pages acceptable to expert referees.

problems.title: Short Riemann
problems.words: Shrink the 2026 machine-checked Riemann proof drastically.
problems.math: Give a Lean 4 proof of `RiemannHypothesis` in at most 10,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

problems.title: Turning a hat by 60 degrees
problems.words: Rotate a hat tile continuously by 60° inside a region of least possible area. Find that area.
problems.math: Determine $\inf\{|E|: E\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the trace of a continuous rigid motion carrying the unit hat to its rotation by $60^\circ$ about a point$\}$, and whether it is attained.

problems.title: Potts transition on hats
problems.words: Show the q-state Potts model on the hat tiling has a discontinuous transition for large q, and a continuous one for q = 2.
problems.math: Prove the $q$-state Potts model on the hat graph has a first-order transition for all $q\ge q_0$ and a continuous one for $q=2$; find the least such $q_0$.

problems.title: Hat tiling heat kernel constant
problems.words: For a random walk on a hat tiling, find the exact constant in the return probability.
problems.math: Prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim\frac{c(o)}{n}$ on the hat graph and show $\frac1{|B_R|}\sum_{o\in B_R}c(o)\to c$ with $c=\frac{\bar d}{2\pi\sqrt{\det\Sigma}}$, computing $\Sigma$ in closed form.

problems.title: Largest factor ratio of consecutive primes
problems.words: For consecutive primes p < q, compare the largest prime factors of p − 1 and q − 1. Show each is larger half the time.

problems.title: Yang–Mills on hats
problems.words: Lattice gauge theory placed on a hat tiling should still have a mass gap at strong coupling and at weak coupling.
problems.math: Prove the $SU(2)$ lattice gauge theory on the 3D product of the hat complex and $\mathbb{Z}$ has a mass gap for all couplings.

problems.title: Hearing the hat
problems.words: Show no other polygon has exactly the same vibration frequencies as the hat.
problems.math: Prove the hat polygon is Dirichlet-spectrally determined among all simply connected polygons.

problems.title: Gerver sofa and the circle
problems.words: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a rational combination of π and 1.
problems.math: Prove $\mu_G\notin\mathbb{Q}+\mathbb{Q}\pi$.

problems.title: Hat Neumann eigenvalue is transcendental
problems.words: Show the first nonzero frequency of an insulated hat-shaped membrane is transcendental.
problems.math: Prove the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue $\mu_2$ of the hat polygon (unit kite side) is transcendental.

problems.title: Gerver sofa eigenvalue is transcendental
problems.words: Show the lowest vibration frequency of a drum shaped like Gerver's sofa is transcendental.
problems.math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of Gerver's sofa is transcendental.

problems.title: Spectre drum eigenvalue is transcendental
problems.words: Show the lowest frequency of a drum shaped like the curved spectre tile is transcendental.
problems.math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spectre domain is transcendental.

problems.title: Lorenz dimension is irrational
problems.words: Show the Hausdorff dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor is irrational.
problems.math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $\dim_H(\mathcal{A})\notin\mathbb{Q}$.

problems.title: Graceful forests with one big tree
problems.words: A forest with c trees and m edges is graceful-forest labelled if its vertices get the labels 0 to m + c − 1 with all edge differences distinct. Show this works whenever there are at least two trees and one of them holds more than half the edges.
problems.math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges and $c\ge2$ components, one of which has more than $m/2$ edges, has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with all $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E$, distinct.
